maya (Eng): Quick question- turned 50 this year and want to start catch-up 401(k) contributions midyear. Also enrolled in HSA via payroll. Can I change deferral to add catch-up midyear and how do HSA pretax deductions interact if I increase deferral? Any vendor forms?

rebecca-peopleops: Congrats on 50+! You can opt into catch-up contributions anytime while employed. Make the change in Workday before payroll cutoff and it applies going forward. Catch-up counts toward the catch-up limit, not the standard deferral limit.

jon-payroll: Practical note: payroll needs the election by 17:00 PT two business days before a pay run. HSA deductions are separate pre-tax elections; increasing 401(k) deferrals won't automatically change HSA amounts. If you want to free up cash for HSA, adjust HSA deferral in Workday too.

elena-hr: Employer match rules unchanged. If the match calculation depends on 'salary deferrals' vs 'compensation', we can confirm specifics for your plan. Reach out if you want us to check the math.

sam (Cornerstone Retirement): Cornerstone note: catch-up contributions are allowed midyear. If you plan to max both standard and catch-up, we recommend checking projected payrolls so you don't exceed limits. Send questions to retirement@cornerstone.com and include last 4 SSN for faster help.

maya (Eng): If I increase percent now, can I later reduce it within the same year?

rebecca-peopleops: Yes, you can change deferral percent multiple times while employed. Remember the payroll cutoff. We'll also run a quick projection if you want to see how many paychecks remain to reach the catch-up target.

benefits-bot: Reminder: 401(k) and HSA election changes: enter in Workday by 17:00 PT two business days before payroll. HSA vendor: https://intranet.redwood/hr/hsa-fsa. 401(k) limits: https://intranet.redwood/hr/401k-limits

maya (Eng): Thanks  please run a projection and I'll submit the Workday changes today. Appreciate it!
